full_judgment:
3. The defendant-petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement. The case of the defendants is that the land in question belongs to the Government and the same was properly recorded as khas land in both SA record as well as RS record. The plaintiff fraudulently obtained ex parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1973 and the defendant filed another Title Suit being Title Suit No.151 of 1975 and obtained a decree to the effect that the judgment and decree passed in Miscelaneous Case No.21 of 1973 is not binding upon the defendant-petitioner. Further case of the defendant is that the land in question is a channel as per section 20(2A) of the SAT Act, 1950 and, as such, the suit land is retainable by the Government and the plain- tiff has miserably failed to prove his possession and the documents as adduced by the plaintiff are forged, collusive and illegal. 

 11. On perusal of the judgment of the lower Appellate Court, we do not find that the lower appellate Court misread the material evidence or misinterpreted on misread the relevant law affecting the merit of the case. Mere entry in the record of right shall not create right and title over any property without any corroborative evidence and materials and this proposition of law gets support from the view taken by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. In the instant case, the petitioner respondent except producing the copies of SA and RS records failed to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land in any manner. Further, it appears. that though the Government raised law point regarding section 20 of the SAT Act 1950 but the DW in his deposition stated that the land is not land and also exhibits have been prepared in that manner and admittedly as per CS record the nature of land in nal.
